subject: Post-call: finalize streaming measurement & remedy language for AcuityHealth pilot

Subject: Post-call: finalize streaming measurement & remedy language for AcuityHealth pilot

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed on related to performance measurement and SLA language for the pilot: 

1) Measurement scope: define how we measure streaming latency (TTFB vs completion), tokens accounted, and concurrency behavior for websocket/HTTP-stream. See attached draft with proposed language (Acuity_SLA-draft-v1.docx) and our measurement definitions CSV.
2) Reporting cadence: monthly SLA report + immediate notification for any incident that looks like a potential SLA breach (within 48 hours).
3) Remedies: provisional wording we discussed — tiered service credits tied to percentage of time below SLO; we left the exact caps open for legal.
4) Exclusions: maintenance windows and customer-side request throttling will be excluded; need to confirm schedule for planned maintenance windows on your side.

Action items I/O:
- Priya: confirm whether Acuity will accept our definition of "streaming completion latency" vs you prefer time-to-last-byte to be the primary metric (due Jun 12).
- Ben/Karthik: incorporate the exchanges and produce tight SLA language with a sample credit calc by EOD Jun 11.

I've attached the working SLA doc and the CSV with metric formulas. We're trying to keep the pilot contract small but explicit on measurement so we can avoid surprises during load testing next week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifying Qs before we sign off on a measurement definition: 

- For streaming, can you confirm whether Redwood will report both time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and time-to-last-token (completion latency)? Our product team cares about TTFB for perceived interactivity but our compliance folks want the completion metric for billing/throughput. We'll likely need both surfaced in the report.
- Regarding concurrency: how will you define a concurrent session (per websocket connection vs per request)? We run bots that open persistent connections and also spike via short-lived HTTP streams — we need the SLA to reflect both patterns.
- Exclusions: we agree to planned maintenance being excluded, but please propose a blackout definition (e.g., >30 min scheduled window notified 72 hours in advance). Also flagging that our security team may request SOC evidence before final sign-off.

Finally, for remedies: can you propose a simple example of how a credit would be calculated for a single monthly measurement (we prefer a predictable formula)?

Thanks — I'll loop in our infra owner if you need schedule windows.

— Priya
Priya Mehta
Head of Platform Reliability, AcuityHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Mehta <priya.m@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: finalize streaming measurement & remedy language for AcuityHealth pilot

Hi Priya — quick answers and a concrete proposal so legal/infra can see a working example. I'll summarize then attach the redline we talked about.

Measurement proposal (short):
- Latency definitions:
  * Time-to-first-byte (TTFB): time from request arrival at Redwood gateway to first non-empty data frame emitted to the client. Report p50/p95 for TTFB.
  * Completion latency: time from request arrival at gateway to final token/frame emitted and acknowledged by the client. Report p95/p99 for completion latency.
- Token accounting: tokens are counted from the model input and streaming output as measured by our tokenizer at the gateway. We will include both input and output tokens in the monthly usage report; pilot pricing remains on total output tokens.
- Concurrency: a concurrent session is defined as an active websocket or active streaming HTTP connection. Short-lived HTTP streams (<= 10s) are included; spikes are measured by 1-minute moving-window concurrency so short bursts are captured.
- Throughput: measured as tokens/sec per model instance as observed by our serving runtime during the measurement window; we will include average and 95th-percentile throughput on the report.

Exclusions & windows:
- Planned maintenance exclusion: any maintenance window > 30 minutes that has been mutually scheduled and notified at least 72 hours in advance. Emergency maintenance will be reviewed case-by-case; we propose it be a separate exclusion only if Redwood notified within 4 hours and posted root cause to the incident timeline.

Remedies (example formula):
- For each monthly measurement period, if the agreed SLO (e.g., completion latency p95 <= X ms) is violated, service credit = min( monthly invoice * breach_ratio * 1.0, monthly invoice * 0.30 ) where breach_ratio = (time_below_SLO_minutes / total_billable_minutes). Example: if 120 minutes of a 43,200-minute month were below SLO, breach_ratio = 0.00278; credit = monthly_invoice * 0.00278 (capped at 30%).
- Notification & dispute: Redwood will provide the measurement dataset + report within 5 business days of period end; Acuity has 15 business days to dispute with supporting logs. Credits will be applied to the next invoice if agreed.

Reporting cadence:
- Monthly SLA report with both raw measurement CSV (attachment) and a one-page executive summary. Immediate incident notification within 48 hours for any event likely to cause an SLA breach.

I've attached a redlined excerpt (Acuity_SLA-draft-v1.docx) and the measurement-definitions-v2.csv with formula fields filled out. If this looks good, Marissa will push these changes into the contract template and we can route for Acuity legal review.

Thanks,
Ben

Priya — following Ben's concrete proposal above, a few housekeeping items and next steps: 

- We've produced the sample credit calc you requested (see Ben's example). If Acuity prefers a simpler fixed-tier credit we can draft that as an alternate — let us know preference by EOD Mon Jun 14.
- On metrics: Redwood will include both TTFB (p50/p95) and completion latency (p95/p99) in the monthly report. We'll also surface concurrency percentiles and throughput (tokens/sec).
- Planned maintenance: we will adopt your blackout definition (>=30 min notified 72 hours prior) unless you propose otherwise.
- Deliverables & timeline: Redwood will: (1) push redlined SLA into the contract template (Marissa) by Mon Jun 14; (2) run a non-production load test Wed Jun 16 to validate measurement hooks (Karthik); (3) produce first month sample report after the test for your review (Ben).

Please confirm the maintenance schedule you expect over the pilot period and whether Acuity legal needs any additional standard clauses up front. If we get a quick signoff on the measurement text, we can lock the pilot start for Jun 22.

If you prefer, I can set a 30-min session next week with our infra folks (Karthik + Ben) and your platform owner.

Best,
Marissa
